Skid Steers at a Glance

When exploring your options, skid steers are easy to identify by their compact size, hydraulic lift arms, and ability to handle a variety of attachments. The most common attachment you’ll encounter—and likely use—is the bucket, perfect for scooping, digging, and moving heavy materials. If your task requires something different, consider the job at hand and choose the attachment that best suits your needs.

One major advantage of skid steers is their exceptional maneuverability. Equipped with either wheels or tracks, these machines can operate in tight spaces and handle rugged terrain with ease. Tracks, in particular, offer enhanced stability and durability, allowing you to navigate uneven ground while minimizing wear and tear. Skid steers also have zero-turn capabilities, making it simple to achieve precise positioning without wasting time on awkward adjustments.

You’ll find skid steers available in a range of sizes, from compact models ideal for small-scale landscaping to larger machines suited for heavy-duty construction work. No matter the size or scope of your project, there’s a skid steer that’s up to the task.

Attachments

Skid steer attachments expand the versatility of these machines far beyond just moving dirt. While the bucket is the go-to attachment for most jobs, there are many other options to consider. For moving large, bulky materials, grapplers are a great choice. Need to dig post holes? Try an auger. Breaking up concrete? A hydraulic breaker is your best friend. With such a wide array of attachments available, there’s almost nothing a skid steer can’t handle.

Now it’s time to explore the possibilities in person. At Glencoe Equipment, we offer a variety of skid steers for sale. Stop by today and let us help you find the right equipment for your needs. We proudly serve customers from Baton Rouge and Prairieville, Louisiana!
